data.title: Dietary protein governs the role of insulin signaling in the postprandial regulation of hepatic mTORC1.
data.authors: Kalafut KC; Cormerais Y; Cissé MY; Lapp SC; Inouye KE; Hotamışlıgil GS; Manning BD

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: In liver-specific mouse genetic models, AKT-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation is the main route by which insulin induces hepatic mTORC1, but is dispensable for feeding-induced activation; postprandial mTORC1 activation instead requires dietary protein, and hepatic mTORC1 signalling is not elevated in diet-induced obesity despite impaired insulin/glucose homeostasis.
data.abstract_excerpt: The nutrient-sensing mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling pathway controls cellular and organismal growth and metabolism, and aberrant activation is linked to human disease, including metabolic disease. Cellular studies have established regulatory mechanisms influencing mTORC1 activation, but the physiological signals that control mTORC1 at the organismal and tissue levels are less well-defined. mTORC1 is dynamically regulated by fasting and feeding in metabolic tissues, with both nutrients and insulin proposed to activate mTORC1 in response to feeding.

extracted_findings.intervention: Liver-specific AKT and TSC2 genetic manipulation; dietary protein and feeding/fasting manipulation
extracted_findings.target: Hepatic mTORC1 via the AKT-TSC2 axis
extracted_findings.effect: AKT-TSC2 phosphorylation is the main insulin route to hepatic mTORC1 but is dispensable for feeding-induced activation, which instead requires dietary protein; hepatic mTORC1 was not elevated in diet-induced obesity.
